title: Scout result
description: What one scout returns for its assigned units: one element per unit, so coverage evidence stays attached to the unit it was gathered for. A scout with one unit returns one element. The orchestrator derives each unit's status from its element (candidates -> candidate, checks only -> covered, neither -> blocked), stamps each check with the scout's agent id, the run id, and the wave, and mints board ids; the scout never does. Read by scout prompts and the workflow graph.

results.description: One element per assigned unit. A unit missing here was not scouted: it stays planned for the next wave, it is never marked covered.

unit.description: The assigned unit id (<surface ref>::<boundary ref>), exactly as given.

checks.description: Coverage evidence for THIS unit only: one entry per invariant decided, either way. Every threat class assigned to the unit gets at least one check (a class that turns out not to apply is a check too: its result says why); the orchestrator lists an assigned class with no check as unchecked.

class.description: The threat class id the check decides (threat-classes.md or ai-and-llm.md heading id, e.g. INJ, AUTHZ-OBJ, AI-TOOL).

candidates.description: Candidates found in this unit, each with the fields of candidate.schema.json except the board id (the orchestrator mints it); unit equals this element's unit.

uncovered.description: Surfaces seen but not checked; they become candidate units for the critic.

hardening_notes.description: Defense-in-depth advice with no reachable boundary violation; never a candidate.

blocked_reason.description: Why the unit could not be checked (unreadable paths, out of scope); set only when checks and candidates are both empty.
